paper_title: Why are CSPs Based on Partition Schemes Computationally Hard?
classifications: Theory of computation → Computational complexity and cryptography
statement: time for any c < 2, The challenge here is that the SETH intrinsically requires reductions where one can “simulate” clauses of arbitrary high arity with a very small overhead. This seems difficult for CSP(B ∨= ) and in Theorem 8 we could only produce a reduction from a SAT problem with a linear number of constraints. This assumption cannot be made for SAT since sparsification, the process of reducing an instance to a subexponential number of instances with a linear number of constraints, is not possible for SAT [28]. Another possibility is to use bounds based on the Chromatic Number problem: Jonsson and Lagerkvist [16, Th. 21] have related the time complexity of Allen’s interval algebra with the time complexity of the Chromatic Number problem and obtained concrete lower bounds of the form O∗ (cn ) for a constant c > 1 depending on the complexity of Chromatic Number. Thus, we ask the following: should stronger lower bounds for CSP(B ∨= ) be pursued in the setting of CNF-SAT and the SETH, or are problems of this kind fundamentally closer to e.g. colouring problems?
